notes.title: None of the categories really match...
notes.notes:
There are [b]10 steam awards[/b] nomination category things.  None of them are really a good fit for Creeper World 4.  Or the other way around maybe... you know what I mean.  So I picked one: [b]Most Innovative[/b].  But you say, "yeah, but I've been playing CW since like 2009 back when the earth was young and giants roamed the land".  True.  But those all happened in parallel realities so CW1/2/3/4 are all really just different instances made by the same Knuckle Cracker in different timelines. Ergo the same 'game' and the same innovation. Q.E.D.

But, pick something else... that's fine too.  Let me know in the comments below what you picked.  Also be sure to subscribe and click the notific.... oh, sorry.  Wrong platform. Scratch that last part.

notes.title: Launch Results
notes.notes:
[h3][b]It's just over 48 hours since the Creeper World 4 launch...[/b][/h3]
And things have progressed fantastically well!  Better than my expectations by several fold. It would seem that folks really do like thermodynamics, differential equations, and cellular automata. Who knew! Sales have exceeded every success metric I'm aware of for the first week of an indie title, and we did it in the first few hours.

Sales have been robust, and Steam shows why it is a juggernaut. I think nowhere else in the depth of time has there been a place where a dude could make an interactive bag of math with some colorful graphics on it, and multitudes of smart folks could buy and enjoy that creation.

[b]So thank you for your support, your purchases, your reviews, and existing. Because the world has smart and interesting people like you in it, I can make simulations and pass them off as games.[/b]

[h3][b]Onward to the 1.1 update![/b][/h3]

notes.title: Creeper World 4 Releasing Dec 3, 2020
notes.notes:
I redoubled my efforts and now the Creeper is ready to flood another hundred thousand worlds. [b]Yes.... (fingers stroking chin).... The Creeper culling has returned![/b] Come bear witness to the turning of another galactic page. The end of one (or more?) galactic civilization and the birth of something new. Dec 3, 2020 around 10:05am PST is the time. Be sure to set a reminder for this world ending event. Either way, you won't miss it.

Oh and there are already some sweet custom maps showing up that are ready for day 1. Folks have even implemented gameplay and weapons that I didn't think of... how'd that happen? The game is already out of my control it would seem and I'm the one looking forward to the release so I can play it!

K75 and I will be doing some live streaming shortly after the launch. I've heard its good for buzz. So tell your friends about the launch, especially all of the ones that have YouTube channels with 1+million subscribers.

[b]Four years[/b]. That's what it has taken to create [b]Creeper World 4[/b]. So naturally you get seven sweet missions to try in the demo. Because 7/4's is... Ok. Anyway. As I was saying; You get five story missions so you can get a feel for where our new hero is headed.  And then you get two more missions.  Special missions. notes.title: Why Creeper World s decade-long evolution keeps getting harder
notes.notes:
This is The Mechanic, where Alex Wiltshire invites developers to discuss the difficult journeys they ve taken to make their games. This time, the Creeper World series [official site].

The whole history of the Creeper World series is serendipitous and unintentional, says its creator, Virgil Wall, in his Texan lilt. You know how it goes with these things, one thing led to another.

Creeper World is a singular take on the realtime strategy that Wall has spent the past decade making. Former man of the cloth Kieron Gillen once described the original as the most apocalyptic game I ve played in ages , an RTS about managing constant attritional threat. But it s also a game about simplicity. As Wall puts it, its original purpose was to throw strategy gaming into a crucible and turn up the Bunsen burner as hot as it could get and boil away anything except the essence.

But that s led to 10 years of grappling with a constant problem: how do you design follow-ups to a game that was already boiled down to its essentials?

(more…)

notes.title: Overcoming alien goo in full 3D looks great in Creeper World 4 trailer
notes.notes:
Creeper World is probably one of the more niche real time games series out there, a series about overcoming an endless tide of world-devouring alien goop. Despite the rudimentary visuals, they’re a wonderful games about trying to overcome the dual challenges of an enemy that never stops coming and the logistics needed to fuel a war machine that can never stop fighting. 

Creeper World 4 is on the way, with a trailer releasing yesterday, and it looks like it’s going to be a leg up on the previous games thanks to some fancy new physics simulation for the eponymous fluids. Creeper World 4 stands a chance of breaking the series out into a more mainstream audience, because indie developer Knuckle Cracker is going full 3D. Check out yesterday’s alpha trailer below.

The concept of orbital weapons is especially appealing. You can watch a bunch of informative developer logs (like one about the aforementioned orbital weapons, or one on the new maps) on Knuckle Cracker’s YouTube channel.

You can check out the previous game in the series, Creeper World 3, on Steam. Creeper World 4 also has a page, for those inclined to wishlist. There’s also Knuckle Cracker’s website. Creeper World 4 will release “when done.”

notes.title: Creeper World 4 gloops into the third dimension
notes.notes:
The Creeper World series are strategy games unlike any other, and Sin Vega reckons they have the best monster of any game, even if the title is a bit rubbish. Part tower defence, part traditional RTS, part fluid dynamics sim, I’ve been a fan of Knuckle Cracker’s quirky if utilitarian-looking series for years now. The next game in the series – Creeper World 4 – will be the first to properly delve into the third dimension. With any luck, it’ll bring new depth (figurative or otherwise) to my years-long battle against an endless tide of caustic blue goo. Take a peek at an early trailer below.
